rationale: The original family case describes very early-onset Alzheimer disease with extrapyramidal signs. Limb spasticity and rigidity worsened on a follow-up exam. The clinical report tracked neurological progression without a measured ground-sage exposure.

The Kolkata cohort followed cognition and dementia in people with Parkinson disease. Cogwheel rigidity contributed to diagnostic classification and UPDRS supported motor assessment. The methods and reported outcomes contain no dietary sage measurement or rigidity estimate linked to sage.

The cross-sectional study compared clinic-based daily living tasks and recorded motor UPDRS in people with Parkinson disease without dementia. Cutting food with a sharp utensil was a task in the self-care skills assessment. The authors did not measure the food consumed or link a ground-sage exposure to rigidity.

The analysis included 25 people with Parkinson disease and 21 controls. It used resting-state and task MRI and an Attention Network Test, with motor UPDRS used to characterize participants. The paper provides no dietary covariate or sage-specific rigidity comparison.

The single-patient stroke rehabilitation study measured upper-limb recovery after cycling and repetitive task practice. The Fugl-Meyer score increased by 20 points. Parkinson disease was background for the intervention rationale. The case measured no ground-sage exposure or Parkinson rigidity outcome.

This publication concerns recruitment, enrollment and barriers for a Parkinson virtual house-call study. Of 210 enrollees, 195 were randomized. The eligibility and baseline material addresses access and technology use and supplies no culinary sage comparison or separate rigidity result.

This is a secondary analysis of 1,022 Parkinson participants from the creatine trial. Metabolic syndrome was associated with an additional 0.5-point annual rise on aggregate motor UPDRS (p=.01). Food-level exposure and a separate sage rigidity estimate were absent. Sage Bionetworks appears in an investigator disclosure.

This invited commentary discusses five family caregiver interviews reported in a separate qualitative paper. It covers cultural expectations of family care, adaptation and support. It provides no measured sage exposure or separately scored rigidity and contributes no independent cohort.

The published study follows 49 people with advanced Parkinson disease on intermittent injections or continuous apomorphine. The original methods include joint rigidity in a clinical response assessment. Its comparison concerns apomorphine treatment and supplies no ground-sage exposure.

The article compares Dutch police-recorded domestic violence before and during the pandemic. Its weekly counts are reported incidents of domestic violence. It has no clinical Parkinson fall outcome or sage exposure.

The pediatric case tests cochlear implant and hearing-aid configurations. Tested outcomes include speech perception in noise and localization. The article reports no Parkinson fatigue or fresh sage exposure.

The report compares frontal-cortex pathology in a dementia pugilistica case with other tissues. In the case history, Table 4 separates caregiver-rated apathy from depression and appetite or eating behavior using the Neuropsychiatric Inventory. There is no dried-sage exposure and the apathy observations concern dementia pugilistica.

The study evaluated 49 people with Parkinson disease, including 40 with Parkinson disease dementia. Table 1 reports 39 of the 40 met the apathy criterion and 27 met the separate depression criterion. The report used the Apathy Evaluation Scale and the Montgomery–Asberg Depression Rating Scale. It has no dried-sage exposure or treatment comparison for apathy.

The prospective Alzheimer cohort included 1,171 in its mortality analysis of donepezil and oral or transdermal rivastigmine. The analysis addresses survival and drug covariates. It supplies no separately measured Parkinson apathy outcome or dried-sage exposure.
